question: What is the primary regulatory body responsible for establishing professional standards for nurses in Nigeria?

options.A: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.B: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria
options.D: National Association of Nigerian Nurses and Midwives

explanation: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria regulates the practice and sets the educational and professional standards for all nurses in the country. [learn more](GST321_U1_T21#GST321_U1_T21_h1)

question: Why are formal job performance evaluations essential in clinical healthcare settings?

options.A: They safeguard patient safety and maintain clinical competence
options.B: They replace the need for continuous professional development
options.C: They primarily serve to determine monthly institutional budgets
options.D: They eliminate all forms of workplace conflict among staff

explanation: Systematic evaluations help identify clinical strengths and gaps, ensuring that care delivered to patients meets established safety and quality standards. [learn more](GST321_U1_T21#GST321_U1_T21_h1)

question: An administrative use of a performance appraisal includes making decisions regarding which of the following?
explanation: Administrative decisions such as career advancement, merit increases, and structural personnel changes rely heavily on documented appraisal outcomes. [learn more](GST321_U1_T21#GST321_U1_T21_h2)

question: How do performance appraisals impact the psychological well-being of nursing staff?

options.A: Structured recognition boosts staff morale and organizational commitment
options.B: They routinely create permanent anxiety and clinical burnout
options.C: They decrease the need for open communication with superiors
options.D: They isolate staff members from interprofessional team collaboration

explanation: Acknowledging a nurse's hard work during an appraisal validates their efforts, which increases job satisfaction and loyalty to the healthcare institution. [learn more](GST321_U1_T21#GST321_U1_T21_h2)

question: Which indicator directly reflects a nurse's commitment to patient safety during daily duties?

options.A: Completing administrative tasks outside of scheduled shifts
options.B: Writing lengthy personal reflections in the ward diary
options.C: Consistent reporting of near misses and incident spikes
options.D: Avoiding participation in multidisciplinary ward rounds

explanation: Tracking and reporting near misses or adverse events are core safety metrics that prevent future patient harm. [learn more](GST321_U1_T21#GST321_U1_T21_h3)

question: A nurse manager evaluating clinical competence should place the highest priority on which observable behavior?

options.A: Finishing assigned shift duties faster than any other colleague
options.B: Completing personal administrative paperwork before schedule
options.C: Adhering strictly to aseptic technique during wound dressings
options.D: Displaying attractive handwriting in the patients' care folders

explanation: Clinical competence relies heavily on core technical skills like sterile technique that directly influence patient infection rates and clinical outcomes. [learn more](GST321_U1_T21#GST321_U1_T21_h3)

question: What is the primary advantage of using Behaviorally Anchored Rating Scales (BARS) in evaluations?

options.A: They focus exclusively on the academic qualifications of the staff
options.B: They rely solely on the self-assessment of the junior nurse
options.C: They use specific workplace behaviors to reduce subjective manager bias
options.D: They require zero time investment from the evaluating nursing officer

explanation: BARS link numeric scores to concrete behavioral descriptions, making the evaluation process much more objective. [learn more](GST321_U1_T21#GST321_U1_T21_h4)

question: What makes 360-degree feedback uniquely comprehensive compared to traditional manager-only reviews?

options.A: It focuses exclusively on the disciplinary history of the employee
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for any formal interview session
options.C: It incorporates observations from peers, subordinates, physicians, and patients
options.D: It relies entirely on computerized tracking of hospital electronic records

explanation: By gathering data from multiple perspectives across the healthcare team, 360-degree feedback provides a well-rounded picture of performance. [learn more](GST321_U1_T21#GST321_U1_T21_h4)

question: When does the job performance evaluation cycle ideally begin for a clinical nurse?

options.A: At the start of the employment cycle by setting clear expectations
options.B: Immediately after a serious clinical error has been reported
options.C: On the exact morning of the scheduled annual appraisal interview
options.D: During the final week before the institutional budget is finalized

explanation: Setting clear performance expectations and goals at the beginning of the evaluation period ensures the nurse knows what standards apply. [learn more](GST321_U1_T21#GST321_U1_T21_h5)

question: What is the primary role of a nurse manager during a formal evaluation interview?

options.A: Acting as a strict judge who issues final unappealable verdicts
options.B: Acting as a facilitator who encourages self-reflection and dialogue
options.C: Observing silent compliance without inviting staff feedback
options.D: Focusing exclusively on administrative paperwork and signatures

explanation: An effective manager guides the conversation to encourage the nurse to evaluate their own practice and discuss challenges openly. [learn more](GST321_U1_T21#GST321_U1_T21_h5)

question: What does the halo effect refer to during a performance appraisal?

options.A: Allowing an exceptional rating in one area to influence all other unrelated metrics
options.B: Giving higher scores to nurses who share the same educational background
options.C: Rating every single staff member as substandard due to strict personal values
options.D: Focusing exclusively on clinical incidents that occurred during the last week

explanation: The halo effect clouds judgment by letting one positive trait overshadow everything else, leading to an unearned overall high rating. [learn more](GST321_U1_T21#GST321_U1_T21_h6)

question: A nurse manager gives a staff member poor ratings across all categories simply because the nurse arrived late twice last month, ignoring months of stellar clinical work. This is an example of which appraisal pitfall?
explanation: The horns effect occurs when a single negative characteristic or mistake negatively biases the evaluator's perception of all other performance areas. [learn more](GST321_U1_T21#GST321_U1_T21_h6)

question: Which of the following elements represents the correct focus of the SBIM feedback model?

options.A: General personality criticisms to ensure rapid behavioral change
options.B: Objective behaviors and their impact rather than personal traits
options.C: Reviewing annual financial records rather than bedside nursing duties
options.D: Comparing the employee directly against the weakest ward worker

explanation: The SBIM model focuses on observable actions and their clinical consequences, keeping feedback professional and non-personal. [learn more](GST321_U1_T21#GST321_U1_T21_h7)

question: Why is it necessary to conduct performance feedback interviews in a private, quiet setting?

options.A: It is a legal requirement set by hospital financial auditors
options.B: It ensures that no written documentation is required afterwards
options.C: It minimizes ward interruptions and encourages open, honest dialogue
options.D: It prevents other staff members from learning the employee's salary

explanation: Privacy and freedom from interruptions help the nurse feel safe, respected, and able to discuss sensitive performance issues openly. [learn more](GST321_U1_T21#GST321_U1_T21_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of a Performance Improvement Plan (PIP)?

options.A: To outline clear, time-bound milestones and support to correct skill deficits
options.B: To serve as a formal warning letter that immediately terminates employment
options.C: To calculate the annual bonus allocation for senior hospital executives
options.D: To schedule routine leave rosters for the upcoming festive season

explanation: A PIP provides structured guidance, resources, and timelines to help a struggling nurse achieve expected competency standards. [learn more](GST321_U1_T21#GST321_U1_T21_h8)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical post-evaluation action taken by a healthcare institution?

options.A: Designing targeted in-service training programs based on identified skill gaps
options.B: Ignoring aggregated appraisal scores in favor of random staff selection
options.C: Monitoring progress milestones outlined in individual improvement plans
options.D: Allocating study leave slots for professional advancement

explanation: Institutions use appraisal data purposefully to guide training and resource allocation; ignoring the data defeats the entire purpose of evaluations. [learn more](GST321_U1_T21#GST321_U1_T21_h8)
